clue.text: Winter vehicle, touring grounds, glistened

indicators.note: a vehicle touring the grounds goes round them, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a sled is a vehicle for snow in winter
a park is an area of grounds, as round a stately home

explanation.surface: A sleigh driven around a snowy estate sparkled in the winter light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winter vehicle' suggests a car in the cold, but it is a sled; 'touring' signals one piece going round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine with reflected light, a synonym of sparkle in the past tense.

clue.text: Young man's brought in special service dishes

indicators.note: one piece is brought into the other, going inside it

parts.note: SAS is the Special Air Service, a British army regiment
a lad is a young man; the 's stands for is, joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A young soldier has joined a special forces unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'man's' stands for 'is', so 'brought in' acts on the young man; SAS is Britain's Special Air Service regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes here are prepared foods, of which mixed leaf and vegetable plates are one kind.

clue.text: More than one messenger approaches the Spanish to expel the French?

indicators.note: one piece is driven out and the other takes its place

parts.note: angles are approaches, ways of tackling a problem
le is French for the
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Somebody wonders whether more than one courier approaching Spaniards will drive out the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to expel' swaps LE in ANGLES for EL.
explanation.definitionFit: In scripture these heavenly beings carry God's messages; the Greek root means messenger.

clue.text: Sauce boat enlarged

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
up means increased, as when prices are up

explanation.surface: A gravy boat has been made bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' looks like one gravy jug; Sauce is the definition and boat starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato condiment is a classic table sauce, so the answer is one kind of sauce.

clue.text: Bridge rivals addressed by international partner, primarily

parts.note: in the card game bridge, East and South sit on opposing sides, so E and S are rivals
a letter addressed to someone is sent to them
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A bridge pair faces opponents, chiefly with a foreign partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Primarily means fundamentally or at heart, the same sense as basically.

clue.text: Am I about to start on clean sort of power?

indicators.note: the words Am I go about the next word, wrapping round it
the start of the word clean is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are about to begin using clean energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the words Am I wrap round the next word; 'start on clean' takes its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is often called atomic power, so the adjective describes a kind of energy.

clue.text: Ragged song and dance causes a storm

parts.note: ragged clothing is torn
a song and dance is a fuss, an ado

explanation.surface: A shabby musical number sparks uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song and dance' looks like a performance but is the idiom for a fuss; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating windstorm, so it is one type of storm.

clue.text: Time when a clock gives four rings

definitions.text: Time when a clock gives four rings

parts.words: Time when a clock gives four rings
parts.note: at twelve o'clock at night a striking clock rings many times; the four rings are the hour's peal of chimes before the strike

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the hour at which a clock sounds four times.
explanation.walkthrough: A chiming clock plays the full peal of four quarter-chimes on the hour before striking, most memorably at twelve at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is the hour when the clock chimes and strikes most fully.

clue.text: Order sort of grey coat

indicators.note: the letters are sorted into a new arrangement, playing on sort as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone places an order for a kind of grey jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GREYCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology and classification, an order is a class or grouping of related things.

clue.text: Most brilliant but least serious

definitions.meaning: brightest, giving off the most light
the most frivolous or flippant, as in light reading

explanation.surface: A double definition contrasting brilliance with frivolity.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means bright and also trivial, so its superlative covers both extremes of brightness and frivolity.

clue.text: Typically, you need it when broke but get it when doing well

definitions.text: Typically, you need it when broke but get it when doing well

parts.words: Typically, you need it when broke but get it when doing well
parts.note: when short of money you need a loan from the bank; when you succeed you are given recognition or praise

explanation.surface: A wry observation about what people lack when poor and earn when successful.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two senses: borrowed money, which the broke need, and acknowledgement, which success earns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a loan facility from a lender and praise or recognition for an achievement.

clue.text: Don and Phil breaking up — one may entertain cruise passengers

indicators.note: the two names break apart and their letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Two friends named Don and Phil are splitting up, perhaps a double act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' rearranges DONPHIL; 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pods of these playful marine mammals often swim beside ships, delighting people on sea voyages.

clue.text: Deployed in fresco, a tin-glazed veneer

indicators.note: the letters are laid out within the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: Describing a technique where fresco and tin glaze are used together as a decorative finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deployed in' signals the answer sits inside frescO A TINGlazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin outer layer laid over a surface, just like a covering layer of paint or glaze.

clue.text: What happens in theatre company's first combined effort

indicators.note: the company's piece comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: surgery takes place in an operating theatre, so an operation is what happens there

explanation.surface: A drama troupe's debut is a group effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Working together towards a shared goal is a joint endeavour, a synonym of teamwork.

clue.text: Boy of 11 — he's poor, going astray, one thinks

parts.note: the boy named in the clue at 11 across is Phil

indicators.note: the letters wander off from their places and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eleven-year-old boy from a poor family is getting into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy of 11' points to the other clue's Phil, not an age; 'going astray' rearranges HESPOOR into OSOPHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinker devoted to questions of reason and existence is a professional deep thinker.

clue.text: A crime solved while in New World

indicators.note: a solved puzzle is worked out, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as he spoke'

explanation.surface: A crime is cleared up while in the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' rearranges ACRIME into AMERIC; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The New World is the name Europeans gave to the western hemisphere's two continents.

clue.text: Leaving out with son asleep

parts.note: kipping is British slang for sleeping

explanation.surface: A child is being left behind while fast asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Kip is informal British for a nap, so kipping means sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to omit or pass over it, like jumping past a page.

clue.text: Mock gross judge

parts.note: to gross a sum is to earn or make it before deductions
to judge something so is to believe or consider it

explanation.surface: Someone is ridiculing a disgusting magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' and 'gross' look like a verb and an adjective about a judge; here mock is an adjective meaning pretend, and gross is the verb to earn.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock battle is a pretend or imitation one, so mock as an adjective means imaginary or feigned.

clue.text: Raised issue with party girl: when does she sleep?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to emit is to issue, give out
a deb, short for debutante, is a girl making her entrance into society parties

explanation.surface: Someone asks a sociable girl when she ever gets any sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses EMITDEB in a down entry. The definition fits the surface's question.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour for retiring for the night is when a person goes to sleep.

clue.text: More like a nobleman, apparently, of a previous time

definitions.meaning: a jokey comparative of earl, a nobleman, as if earl were an adjective

explanation.surface: Someone seems more aristocratic, as if from an older era.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: adding the comparative ending to a noble title makes 'more earl-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior or sooner in time, the comparative of early, means belonging to a previous time.

clue.text: Spirited fourth phase of play requires energy

parts.note: a phase of a stage play is an act
IV is four in Roman numerals, as in Act IV
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The fourth stage of a drama demands vigour from the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means lively and energetic, the same as being full of vigour.

clue.text: Lay out, half dressed?

definitions.meaning: to spend money in expectation of a return
read as two words, wearing only an undershirt, so only partly clothed

explanation.surface: A double definition, one straight and one cryptic.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN VEST, the answer describes someone wearing just a vest, a sleeveless undershirt in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out money is to spend it hoping for profit, as when buying shares.

clue.text: Perform like Eminem, casually fast

parts.note: Eminem is a famous rapper, so performing like him is to rap
doing something casually is doing it idly, without effort

explanation.surface: Advice to deliver lyrics in the laid-back, quick-fire style of the rapper Eminem.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, fast means at speed, a direct synonym of quickly.

clue.text: Fair to refine tin from Congo?

indicators.note: refining reworks the material, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: a tin is a can, as in a tin of beans

explanation.surface: A suggestion that it is reasonable to smelt tin ore mined in the Congo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to refine' rearranges FAIR into AFRI; the question mark marks Congo as one example of the continent's countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Congo is a country on that continent, so something from there belongs to the continent, shown by example.

clue.text: Emergency rules I — Sir Chris — will hold over

indicators.note: in this down-pointing sense, over means the held letters are turned round and read backwards
the run of words holds the letters inside it, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A cycling champion, Sir Chris Hoy perhaps, announces he will keep a ruling in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will hold' finds ruleS I SIR Chris; 'over' reverses SISIRC.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a time of intense danger or difficulty, a synonym of a critical turning point.

clue.text: Note written by one's European shrink

indicators.note: one piece is written beside the next, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
one is I, and one's is read as I'S, I with S

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist from Europe has written a short note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' is slang for a psychiatrist in the surface, but here it is the verb to reduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce something to the smallest possible amount is to make it shrink, a synonym of lessen.

clue.text: Heard team were breathing heavily

indicators.note: what is heard is a spoken word, so a word for team is said out loud

parts.note: a side is a team, as in a football side

explanation.surface: Listeners noticed the players panting after hard exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out heavily in weariness or relief is to let out a long audible breath, the past-tense verb.

clue.text: Gin rates poorly, and most bitter

indicators.note: the words are done poorly, put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A disappointed drinker gives the gin a bad review and is very resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges GINRATES; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter in the sense of resentful matches very cross, and the superlative form fits most bitter.
